### [Read the docs →](https://bun.aphrody.app/docs)

## What is Bun OS?

Bun OS brings the [Bun](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun) toolkit and Aphrody's native integrations together in the `bun` executable. Run JavaScript and TypeScript, install packages, test applications and bundle code with the same command. The runtime uses Rust and JavaScriptCore, with C++ bindings to WebKit.

```sh
bun run index.tsx              # run TypeScript and JSX
bun install                    # install package.json dependencies
bun test                       # run application tests
bun build ./app.tsx --outdir dist
```

Bun OS declares native system, Python, .NET, graph and desktop integration surfaces. The [runtime reference](https://bun.aphrody.app/runtime) records their source contracts and platform requirements. Availability requires evidence for the selected executable and target; a source declaration alone does not qualify behavior.

## Features beyond upstream Bun

This source is upstream [oven-sh/bun](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun) 1.4.4 (`bun-v1.4.4`) plus the fork features the `bun` executable links. The [feature catalog](https://bun.aphrody.app/docs/runtime/fork-features) lists every command, `Bun.*` API, `bun:*` module, package, agent tool and skill that Bun OS adds, with the source that owns each. Highlights: native `bun check`, `bun lint`, `bun fmt` and `bun n2b`; `bun mcp`, `bun lsp` and `bun agent-plugin` for coding agents; `bun ssh`, `bun docker`, `bun vpn` and `bun host`; `bun:python`, `bun:dotnet`, `bun:windows`, `bun:winrt`, `bun:winui` and `bun:linux`; `Bun.Video`, `Bun.HTML`, `Bun.Crawl` and `bun:chromium`; `bun wasm`; and the Bun WebOS desktop with the self-hosted `aphrody` server.

The add-ons live in their own repositories: the `uv`, `vpn`, `ssh`, `docker`, `just` and `winmd` plugins, which `bun` downloads on first use, and Bun Video. This checkout mounts them as optional submodules, so a clone stays light. [Add-ons](https://bun.aphrody.app/docs/project/add-ons) covers installing them, building them from source and where their issues go.

## Bun.Video

The flagship native media API reads metadata, extracts frames and applies the `Bun.Image` pipeline directly in TypeScript. Frame batches, WAV audio, GIF output and MP4 remux use native Rust workers.

```ts
const video = new Bun.Video("clip.mp4");
const metadata = await video.metadata();
await video.frame(1).resize(320, 180).webp().write("preview.webp");
```

Read the [Bun.Video reference](https://bun.aphrody.app/docs/runtime/video) for codec support, resource limits and platform requirements. The optional [Bun Video package](https://github.com/aphrody-labs/bun-video) adds composition engines, HLS/DASH and FFmpeg/mpv adapters.

Source version: **1.4.4**. Immutable release source: [852e68acc5d64a6f688961e91ea150d67dceb254](https://github.com/aphrody-labs/bun/tree/852e68acc5d64a6f688961e91ea150d67dceb254). Published downloads and checksums identify available executables. This source revision requires its own native factory and runtime qualification.

## Install

The installers select an already published runtime for your platform. Check [downloads and checksums](https://bun.aphrody.app/downloads) for available targets; these commands do not publish or qualify this source revision.

```sh
# Linux and macOS
curl -fsSL https://bun.aphrody.app/install | bash

# Windows (PowerShell)
powershell -c "irm bun.aphrody.app/install.ps1 | iex"

# Published runtime package
bun add --global @aphrody/bun-runtime
```

The [Windows installer](https://github.com/aphrody-labs/bun/tree/852e68acc5d64a6f688961e91ea150d67dceb254/scripts/aphrody/install.ps1) accepts `-BinDir` or `APHRODY_BUN_BIN_DIR`. User state and caches live under `BUN_INSTALL`.

### Upgrade

```sh
bun upgrade
```

Upgrades select published Bun OS releases. Build the checkout with `bun bd` and test its executable with `bun bd test <file>` when working on Bun OS itself.

## Native quality and migration

Use `bun check`, `bun lint`, `bun fmt` and `bun n2b` directly for type checking, lint, formatting and migration. These commands use their linked native owners; external subprocess backends, standalone Oxc tools, tsgo/tsc and external n2b are not permitted for these tasks. Package scripts may expose these native commands but must not wrap or replace them; `bunx` is reserved for unrelated packages.

Qualify checkout changes with `bun bd check`, `bun bd lint`, `bun bd fmt` and `bun bd n2b`. Native failures must be corrected in their owner.

## Packages and native imports

Dedicated SDK catalogs: [Google REST and Cloud Code](packages/bun-google/README.md),
[Chromium and Chrome CDP](packages/bun-chromium/README.md). Their package guides
include commands, runtime requirements and dedicated agent documentation.

First-party npm packages use the `@aphrody` scope: [`@aphrody/bun-runtime`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@aphrody/bun-runtime), [`@aphrody/bun-types`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@aphrody/bun-types) and [`@aphrody/bun-plugin-tailwind`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@aphrody/bun-plugin-tailwind). Rust plugin crates retain their manifest names: [`aphrody-bun-native-plugin`](https://crates.io/crates/aphrody-bun-native-plugin) and [`aphrody-bun-macro`](https://crates.io/crates/aphrody-bun-macro). Source manifests and registry publication are separate inventories.

Built-in imports keep the Bun ABI and module names:

```ts
import { $ } from "bun";
import { Database } from "bun:sqlite";
import { expect, test } from "bun:test";
```

## Release surfaces

Run `bun run release:surfaces --out <absolute-directory>` from a committed checkout. README, GitHub metadata, agent plugin bundles and static site share the same immutable Git source. `manifest.json` records every generated artifact's SHA-256. Use `--apply` to update the tracked README and GitHub metadata. Network release inventory is captured separately from source facts; `--offline` generates without published-release claims.
